b2-bartokkodaly-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Wax Cylinders
b2-bartokkodaly-01.scenario: At the Institute for Musicology in Budapest, a guide shows you an old wax cylinder and asks how Kodály and Bartók recorded the village singers.
b2-bartokkodaly-01.prompt: Tell her what the two composers took to the villages and what they did with the recordings in the evenings.
cues: Say what they took to the villages
Say what they did in the evenings
b2-bartokkodaly-01.target: Bartók és Kodály fonográfot vittek a falvakba, és az idős énekesek dalait viaszhengerekre vették. Esténként türelmesen kérdezgették a falusiakat, és rendszerezgették a felvételeket.
b2-bartokkodaly-01.english: Bartók and Kodály took a phonograph to the villages and recorded the old singers' songs on wax cylinders. In the evenings they patiently asked the villagers around and sorted the recordings bit by bit.
b2-bartokkodaly-01.canDo: I can describe how Bartók and Kodály recorded peasant singers using Edison wax cylinders.

b2-bartokkodaly-02.title: Communicative Challenge: City Song, Village Song
b2-bartokkodaly-02.scenario: At a music-history talk in Budapest, a student asks how the old village songs differ from the magyar nóta heard in the city cafés.
b2-bartokkodaly-02.prompt: Tell her what the city public believed and what kind of scale Bartók found in the mountain villages of Csík.
cues: Say what the city public believed about the nóta
Say what Bartók found in the villages
b2-bartokkodaly-02.target: A városi közönség azt hitte, hogy a magyar nóta ősi népzene. Bartók viszont a hegyi falvakban üldögélve ötfokú, pentaton dallamokat hallgatott.
b2-bartokkodaly-02.english: The city public believed that the magyar nóta was ancient folk music. Bartók, however, sitting in the mountain villages, listened to five-tone, pentatonic melodies.
b2-bartokkodaly-02.canDo: I can explain the difference between 19th-century urban magyar nóta and ancient pentatonic peasant songs.

b2-bartokkodaly-03.title: Communicative Challenge: From Village to Concert Hall
b2-bartokkodaly-03.scenario: In the foyer of a concert hall in Budapest, a friend asks how Bartók's travels in the villages show in his music.
b2-bartokkodaly-03.prompt: Tell her how Bartók collected the songs and what Judit does in A kékszakállú herceg vára.
cues: Say how Bartók travelled while collecting
Say what Judit does in the opera
b2-bartokkodaly-03.target: Bartók faluról falura járogatott, és az ősi dallamokat beépítette a zenéjébe. A kékszakállú herceg várában Judit ajtóról ajtóra nyitogatja a kamrákat.
b2-bartokkodaly-03.english: Bartók went from village to village and built the ancient melodies into his music. In Bluebeard's Castle, Judit opens the chambers door by door.
b2-bartokkodaly-03.canDo: I can explain how Bartók integrated folk rhythms and pentatonic intervals into modern classical masterpieces.

b2-bartokkodaly-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Music for Everyone
b2-bartokkodaly-04.scenario: At a school open day in Hungary, a parent asks why the children sing and use hand signs instead of starting on a piano or violin.
b2-bartokkodaly-04.prompt: Explain Kodály's idea and how the children practise the intervals.
cues: Say how the children practise the intervals
b2-bartokkodaly-04.target: Kodály szerint a zene mindenkié, és az énekhang mindenkinek a torkában ott van. A gyerekek napról napra kézjelekkel mutogatják a hangközöket.
b2-bartokkodaly-04.english: According to Kodály, music belongs to everyone, and the singing voice is in everybody's throat. Day by day the children practise showing the intervals with hand signs.
b2-bartokkodaly-04.canDo: I can explain Zoltán Kodály's philosophy ('Legyen a zene mindenkié!') and relative solmization.

b2-bartokkodaly-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Dance House
b2-bartokkodaly-05.scenario: At a táncház in Budapest, a first-time visitor asks how the young people learned the dances of Szék.
b2-bartokkodaly-05.prompt: Tell him how the young people learned the steps and who helped them.
cues: Say how the young people learned the steps
b2-bartokkodaly-05.target: A fiatalok lépésről lépésre próbálgatták a széki táncot. Az idősebb táncosok türelmesen javítgatták a tartásukat.
b2-bartokkodaly-05.english: Step by step the young people kept trying out the dance of Szék. The older dancers patiently kept adjusting their posture.
b2-bartokkodaly-05.canDo: I can explain how the 1970s Budapest Táncház movement revived living Transylvanian folk dance and music.

b2-bartokkodaly-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Bartók, Kodály and the Táncház
b2-bartokkodaly-consolidation.scenario: At the Institute for Musicology, a foreign guest asks you for a short summary of how Bartók and Kodály changed Hungarian music.
b2-bartokkodaly-consolidation.prompt: Give a short summary: the fieldwork, Kodály's idea and the táncház.
cues: Say how the two composers collected the songs
Say what Kodály wanted for children
b2-bartokkodaly-consolidation.target: Bartók és Kodály faluról falura járogatva gyűjtötték a népdalokat. Kodály szerint a zene mindenkié, ezért a gyerekek kézjelekkel tanulnak. A táncház az 1970-es években újra élővé tette a hagyományt.
b2-bartokkodaly-consolidation.english: Going from village to village, Bartók and Kodály collected the folk songs. According to Kodály music belongs to everyone, so children learn with hand signs. In the 1970s the táncház made the tradition live again.
b2-bartokkodaly-consolidation.canDo: I can explain the ethnomusicological revolution of Bartók and Kodály, from wax-cylinder fieldwork and pentatonic discovery to modernist composition, the Kodály Concept, and the Táncház revival.
